title: Proteomic analysis in wild bilberry (Vaccinium myrtillus L.) during fruit ripening
projectDescription: The study investigated protein dynamics throughout fruit developmental and ripening process of blue-colored bilberry. The proteomic approach was applied to study at four different ripening stages, S2-small green fruit, S3- large green fruit, S4- purple ripening fruit, S5- ripe, blue fruit of bilberry. Regulatory network of plant hormones and physiological processes occurring during bilberry fruit ripening was revealed for the first time. The white-colored mutant bilberry, at the ripe stage, was also investigated differences compared to wild, blue-colored berries.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Berries of wild bilberry at 4 different ripening stages (S2-S5), and ripe, white-colored mutant were collected during summer from the natural forest standing in Oulu, Finland (65◦03′37.0′′N 25◦28′30.4′′ E). Three biological replicates for each ripening stage were used in the analysis. Proteins were extracted from the pellet generated during metabolite extraction from 100mg freeze-dried fine powder berries according to Salem et al. (2016). The pellets after removing all the solution were washed with methanol and centrifuged at 20,000 g for 10 min at 4oC, four times. The washed pellets were dried at RT and extracted with 500 µl protein extraction buffer consisting of 6M urea, 2M thiourea, 15mM DTT, 2% CHAPS, 1% protease and phosphatase inhibitors. The samples were then sonicated for 10 min, and incubated for 30 min at RT. The protein concentration was determined using Roti®nanoquant (Roth, Germany) following the manufacturer’s instructions. An amount of 100 µg of protein was digested with 500 ng/µl of Trypsin (Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA) at 37oC overnight. The digested proteins were precipitated with four volumes of 100% cold-acetone, at -20oC for 2 hours. Samples were then centrifuged at 14,000 g for 30 min at 4oC. After removing the supernatant, proteins were precipitated once in 80% cold-acetone at -20oC for 1 hour, then centrifuged for 30 min at 4oC. The pellets were dried at RT and digested once with 500 ng/µl of Trypsin overnight at 37oC. The resultant peptides were purified using 100 µl C18 Tips according to the manufacturer’s instructions (Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA). The eluted peptides were dried at RT and re-dissolved in 0.1% formic acid.
dataProcessingProtocol: Thermo Easy-nLC coupled to Orbitrap FusionTM LUMOSTM system (Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA) was used for protein analysis. The UPLC-MS2 run was performed in three technical replicates for each biological sample. A full scan for detecting peptides was set at 375 – 1,500 m/z in the Orbitrap at a resolution of 120,000. The peptides were detected in ddMS2 mode with 30% HCD collision energy, and the first mass was fixed at 110 m/z. The obtained raw data was processed by Protein Discoverer v2.2.038 (Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA). Parameters used for the analysis were as follow: enzyme was trypsin; two miss cleavage sites; mass tolerance of precursor ion was set at 10 ppm, and mass tolerance of fragment ions was set at 0.6 Da; acetylation for N-terminal modification, oxidation of methionine and deamidation of asparagine and glutamine for dynamic modifications, and carbamidomethyl for static modification. The quality of proteins was ensured by removing contaminants and filtering with at least two peptides with a high confidence of false discovery rate of 0.01, and removing outliers. High-quality proteins were identified by searching against three-frame forward translated protein sequences from the bilberry transcriptome (Nguyen et al., 2018) and bilberry protein sequences obtained from a recent study (Wu et al., 2022; https://www.vaccinium.org/bio_data/1085390).
